text:
ops-cust: hitting failures when running the onprem installer — model download step fails and then telemetry/auth also fail. installer logs attached.

sara-support: sorry you're blocked. can you paste the exact failing lines from the installer log and the output of \`curl -v https://model-registry.redwood.internal/v1/models\` from the host where the installer runs? also which network mode (NAT GW, egress proxy) are you using?

ops-cust: using NAT gw with proxy + TLS inspection on egress. installer snippet:\n```
2026-03-15T10:12:34Z ERROR downloader: shard fetch failed: Get "https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood-models/abc.tar.gz": tls: handshake failure
Caused by: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```
curl output from node:\n```
* Rebuilt URL to: https://model-registry.redwood.internal/v1/models
*   Trying 10.0.0.12...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to model-registry.redwood.internal (10.0.0.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection attempt failed: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert handshake failure
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert handshake failure
```

devon-se: thanks — two immediate suspects: 1) TLS inspection/proxy is intercepting SNI/OCSP and breaking cert validation; 2) outbound allowlist missing for package hosts/model shards/auth/telemetry. When TLS intercept is present you often see "certificate signed by unknown authority" or handshake failure.

sara-support: please run these quick checks on the node and paste results:\n1) \`openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood.internal:443 -servername model-registry.redwood.internal -showcerts\`\n2) \`curl -vI https://files.pythonhosted.org/simple/ -H \"Host: files.pythonhosted.org\"\`\n3) \`nslookup model-registry.redwood.internal\`\n

ops-cust: output of openssl shows the proxy cert (internal CA) instead of the real Redwood cert. nslookup resolves to internal NAT IP. curl to files.pythonhosted gives 403 from proxy appliance, not from origin.

devon-se: ok that's consistent with interception. For the installer and runtime we require TLS passthrough or an allowlist exemption for these hostnames so certificate chain is preserved. Minimal outbound allowlist we recommend (TCP 443 unless noted):
- model-registry.redwood.com (auth & model metadata)
- auth.redwood.com, sts.redwood.com (OAuth token endpoints)
- telemetry.redwood.com, metrics.redwood-telemetry.net
- files.pythonhosted.org, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org (pip wheels)
- s3.amazonaws.com and regional S3 endpoints used by your model shard config (e.g., *.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com)
- storage.googleapis.com, *.azureedge.net as applicable for cloud storage backends
- api.github.com (for some installs that pull from releases)
- crl3.digicert.com, ocsp.digicert.com (OCSP/CRL checks)
- kms.amazonaws.com or your KMS endpoints if KMS signing is used
- registry-1.docker.io (if pulling containers)
Also allow DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to your resolver and outbound TCP 443 to the above with SNI preserved.

sara-support: addendum: if you have a TLS proxy that re-signs certificates, make sure it forwards OCSP stapling or configure the proxy to bypass for the above hostnames. Otherwise the installer and model shards that validate certs and KMS will fail.

ops-cust: can you give a one-line firewall rule list I can hand to infra? they want minimal entries.

devon-se: sure — example minimal entries to open from the installer/kube nodes to the internet (egress):
- ALLOW tcp:443 to model-registry.redwood.com
- ALLOW tcp:443 to auth.redwood.com
- ALLOW tcp:443 to telemetry.redwood.com
- ALLOW tcp:443 to files.pythonhosted.org and pypi.org
- ALLOW tcp:443 to *.s3.amazonaws.com (or your configured S3 region)
- ALLOW udp:53 and tcp:53 to your DNS resolver
- ALLOW tcp:443 to crl3.digicert.com and ocsp.digicert.com

Also if your network team requires IPs instead of FQDNs, ask them to resolve the FQDNs and monitor for changes; using FQDN allowlist with SNI-based rules is preferred.

ops-cust: infra pushed the changes and bypassed TLS inspection for the above FQDNs. after that installer progressed but failed later during auth exchange: 401 from auth.redwood.com when fetching service token.

sara-support: can you paste the exact 401 response body (redact tokens) and the time range? we want to see if clock skew or missing client cert is causing it.

ops-cust: 401 body: \n```{\"error\":\"invalid_client\",\"error_description\":\"client credentials not found\"}```\nTime sync looks good (NTP ok).

devon-se: that usually means either outbound IP is not permitted by our token service (we have optional IP allowlists for some enterprise accounts) or the client_id/secret didn't get to the node because our installer couldn't reach the vault/KMS. Can you confirm the installer logs show successful fetch of secrets from your KMS endpoint? also which installer mode (air-gapped vs online)?

ops-cust: online mode. KMS fetch logs show TLS handshake to kms.company.local failed earlier but later succeeded after bypass. the installer seems to retry but the service token exchange still 401.

sara-support: I'm escalating to eng-oncall to double-check token logs for your org and to confirm there's no IP restriction on token issuance. please hang tight.

oncall-eng: hi — I checked auth logs for your organization at 2026-03-15T10:12-10:20Z. We see auth attempts from the public NAT IP X.X.X.123 that returned 401 with error_description \"client credentials not found\" — that indicates the client_id presented doesn't match any registered client for your account. Common cause: proxy rewrote the Authorization header or the installer failed to load credentials from the node. Can you run on the node:\n```
cat /opt/redwood/installer/credentials.json
```
and paste (redact) the client_id value?

ops-cust: client_id present in that file matches the one in our portal. headers look correct in packet capture, no rewrite seen.

devon-se: one last check — ensure outgoing requests to auth.redwood.com are not going via a transparent proxy that strips or reorders chunked headers. Also check there's no corporate WAF dropping requests with the Authorization header. If packet capture shows header present to auth.redwood.com and our logs still 401, please share a sanitized curl reproduce from the node that includes the Authorization header (set placeholders) so we can replay server-side logs.

ops-cust: ran a curl reproduce:\n```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" https://auth.redwood.com/v1/token
```
Response: 401 same body. headers arriving at our appliance show Authorization present; appliance not modifying.

oncall-eng: thanks — I've flagged this for the auth team to inspect with the request_id we correlate from your node (added to the internal ticket). In parallel, please keep TLS bypass in place for the listed FQDNs and ensure any egress proxy allows passthrough for SNI and OCSP. Once auth team has finished, we'll update here.

deploy-bot: support ticket S-2026-4392 created and linked to Eng:auth. ETA initial response 2 hours. :white_check_mark:

ops-cust: thanks all — bypass worked for installer progress; we'll monitor and wait for auth team.

sara-support: leaving this here for the KB: common root causes for installer/model pull failures in private/VPC installs: TLS interception, missing allowlisted FQDNs (pypi, model shards, telemetry, auth), DNS split-horizon resolving to internal IPs, OCSP/CRL blocking, and WAF/proxy header rewriting. Recommend enabling FQDN bypass for our host list and opening tcp/udp 53, tcp 443.

ops-cust: confirmed resolved after auth team fixed a misregistered client_id mapping on their side. installer completed. thanks! :tada:
